rocks.name: Granite
rocks.note: Magma that cooled slowly deep down: coarse grains of quartz, feldspar and mica. The roots of continents and mountains.

rocks.name: Gneiss
rocks.note: Granite and sediment squeezed and heated deep in a mountain belt until its minerals lined up in bands.

rocks.name: Slate
rocks.note: Mudstone baked and pressed in a mountain belt: splits into flat sheets.

rocks.name: Basalt
rocks.note: Lava cooled fast at the surface. The ocean floors, lava fields and volcanic islands.

rocks.name: Andesite
rocks.note: The lava of volcanic arcs above sinking plates.

rocks.name: Tuff
rocks.note: Volcanic ash, settled and welded into rock.

rocks.name: Obsidian
rocks.note: Lava cooled so fast it became glass. Flakes to an edge sharper than steel.

rocks.name: Sandstone
rocks.note: Sand of old beaches, rivers and deserts, buried and cemented.

rocks.name: Shale
rocks.note: Mud settled in quiet water, pressed into thin layers. Where coal seams lie.

rocks.name: Limestone
rocks.note: The shells of sea life, piled up on old sea floors. Water dissolves it into caves.

rocks.name: Coal
rocks.note: Swamp forests buried and pressed for millions of years. Burns hot, with a little sulfur.
